claims.assessment: noted inconsistencies in mourning dress grades

translationRepairs: if the husband is adopted, his wife mourns her birth mother's kin and the wives of younger sons.
if the husband is adopted, his wife mourns his birth parents (as her parents-in-law) and the wives of the younger sons.
In 夫為人後者，其妻為本生舅、姑, 舅、姑 are the wife's parents-in-law and 本生 marks the adopted husband's birth parents, not the wife's maternal kin. The proposed idiomatic wording restores that sense.
when the husband is an adopted son, his wife for her birth mother's brothers and sisters, for the younger sons' wives.
when the husband is an adopted son, his wife for his birth parents (her parents-in-law), and for the younger sons' wives.

Same unit: literal 'her birth mother's brothers and sisters' misreads 本生舅、姑. Here 舅、姑 are parents-in-law and 本生 points to the husband's birth parents; the proposed literal corrects both referent and kinship terms.

Early on Taizong observed that kin eating from one pot wore finest hemp, yet brother's wife and younger brother's husband had no mourning; maternal uncle and aunt were equally close yet dressed differently. He ordered Wei Zheng, Linghu Defen, and others to debate: "The uncle is mother's clan; the aunt is outer kin of another surname—the uncle weighs heavier, yet mourning lasts one season while the aunt's is five months: the ancients missed this.

Early on Taizong observed that kin eating from one pot wore finest hemp, yet elder brother's wife and husband's younger brother had no mourning; maternal uncle and aunt were equally close yet dressed differently. He ordered Wei Zheng, Linghu Defen, and others to debate: "The uncle is mother's clan; the aunt is outer kin of another surname—the uncle weighs heavier, yet mourning lasts one season while the aunt's is five months: the ancients missed this.
嫂叔 is the elder brother's wife (嫂) and the husband's younger brother (叔), not 'younger brother's husband'. Context 弟妻及夫兄 confirms the complementary pair. The proposed idiomatic fix is accurate.

At first Taizong once noted that though they ate from one pot in finest hemp, yet elder brother's wife and younger brother's husband had no mourning dress, and maternal uncle and maternal aunt were equal kin yet different dress; he ordered Palace Attendant Wei Zheng, Vice Minister of Rites Linghu Defen, and others to discuss: "The maternal uncle is mother's clan; the aunt is outer kin of another surname—the uncle is indeed weighty, yet dress lasts only a season, while aunt mourning is five months: the ancients did not penetrate this.

At first Taizong once noted that though they ate from one pot in finest hemp, yet elder brother's wife and husband's younger brother had no mourning dress, and maternal uncle and maternal aunt were equal kin yet different dress; he ordered Palace Attendant Wei Zheng, Vice Minister of Rites Linghu Defen, and others to discuss: "The maternal uncle is mother's clan; the aunt is outer kin of another surname—the uncle is indeed weighty, yet dress lasts only a season, while aunt mourning is five months: the ancients did not penetrate this.
Literal likewise misrenders 叔 in 嫂叔 as 'younger brother's husband'. The replacement 'husband's younger brother' matches the kinship pair and leaves the rest intact.
brother's wife and younger brother's husband: lesser hemp five months, reciprocal;
elder brother's wife and husband's younger brother: lesser hemp five months, reciprocal;
嫂叔服以小功五月報 again names sao and shu (elder brother's wife and younger brother). The following 弟妻及夫兄 pair shows the complementary relation; 'younger brother's husband' is wrong.
elder brother's wife and younger brother's husband, dress in lesser hemp five months, return mourning;
elder brother's wife and husband's younger brother, dress in lesser hemp five months, return mourning;
Same 嫂叔 error in the literal field; 'husband's younger brother' restores the correct reciprocal pair with 嫂.
The court then ordered joint debate on mourning for maternal uncles and for brother's wife and younger brother's husband, but no decision came for a long time.
The court then ordered joint debate on mourning for maternal uncles and for elder brother's wife and husband's younger brother, but no decision came for a long time.
舅及嫂叔服 repeats the same 嫂叔 kinship; the idiomatic 'younger brother's husband' is a real error, and the proposed replacement matches the Chinese.
Then an edict ordered joint deliberation on dress for maternal uncles and elder brother's wife and younger brother's husband; long they could not decide.
Then an edict ordered joint deliberation on dress for maternal uncles and elder brother's wife and husband's younger brother; long they could not decide.
Literal 'younger brother's husband' for 叔 in 嫂叔 is the same mistranslation; 'husband's younger brother' is correct.
Announcer bore tray of water and basket; first to third rank, rice grain for filling, pearls for mouth;
Announcer bore tray of water and basket; first to third rank, fine millet for filling, jade disks for mouth;
飯用粱，唅用璧 specifies fine millet (粱) for filling and jade disks (璧) for the mouth, not rice and pearls. The proposed literal matches the Chinese and the already-correct idiomatic.
Six carts followed in order: exorcist, great coffin, bier, spirit goods, canopy, grain, wine and provisions, wrapped sacrifice, and food carts—then bright banner, great banner, bells, and hearse.

The exorcist, great coffin cart, and bier cart went first; then the spirit-object, lower-canopy, grain, wine-and-provisions, wrapped-sacrifice, and food carts—the six carts—then bright banner, great banner, bells, and hearse in order.
方相、大棺車、輴車 are listed apart from 明器輿…食輿為六輿; the original idiomatic wrongly counts all preceding carts as the six. The proposed wording separates the three lead vehicles from the six 輿.
The guest said: "I, bearing such posthumous title and rank, return to the tomb—I present these gifts."
The guest said: "So-and-so of such posthumous title and enfeoffment, or of such-and-such rank, is about to return to the dark dwelling—I dare present these gifts."
某謚封若某位，將歸幽宅 names the deceased about to be buried; the guest then 敢致賵. The original wrongly makes the guest claim the posthumous title and return to the tomb.
Guest said: "I, posthumous title and enfeoffment or such-and-such rank, return to the dark dwelling—I dare present gifts."
Guest said: "So-and-so of posthumous title and enfeoffment, or such-and-such rank, is about to return to the dark dwelling—I dare present gifts."
Same referent error in the literal: the posthumous title/enfeoffment and return to the dark dwelling belong to the deceased, not the speaking guest.
The guest advanced west of the bier, set the silk on the cart, left westward; the host bowed to the ground in farewell.
The guest advanced east of the bier facing west, set the silk on the cart, left westward; the host bowed to the ground in farewell.
賓進輴東，西面 means the guest advanced to the east of the bier and faced west; 'west of the bier' reverses the side. The proposed idiomatic restores both position and facing.
The host's tablet was mulberry wood one foot by four inches, hole nine fen, in a black-lacquered case west inside the chamber door facing east, with a plain table to the right.
The spirit tablet was mulberry wood one foot by four inches, hole nine fen, in a black-lacquered case west inside the chamber door facing east, with a plain table to the right.
In 主用桑 under the 虞 rite, 主 is the spirit tablet (神主), not the mourning host. Replacing 'The host's tablet' with 'The spirit tablet' corrects the referent.
Host used mulberry, one foot long, four inches square, hole diameter nine fen, black-lacquered case, set at spirit seat west within the chamber door facing east, plain table right.
Spirit tablet of mulberry, one foot long, four inches square, hole diameter nine fen, black-lacquered case, set at spirit seat west within the chamber door facing east, plain table right.
Literal 'Host used mulberry' wrongly makes the host the agent of 主用桑; the phrase specifies the spirit tablet's material. The proposed wording is accurate.
The host's tablet was chestnut wood; offerings followed the yu rite.
The spirit tablet was chestnut wood; offerings followed the yu rite.
主用栗 likewise means the spirit tablet is of chestnut wood, not that the host used chestnut. The proposed idiomatic correction matches ritual usage.
Host used chestnut wood; offering as yu rite.
Spirit tablet of chestnut wood; offering as yu rite.
Same 主 = spirit-tablet sense as at the yu tablet; literal 'Host used chestnut wood' invents the host as agent. The proposed replacement is correct.
Wine jars stood southeast of the hall door, facing west, ranked north to south.
Wine jars stood southeast of the chamber door in the hall, facing north, ranked west to east.
堂上室戶之東南，北向西上 places the jars southeast of the chamber door on the hall, facing north with west superior. The original misreads the doorway as the hall door and reverses facing/ranking.
Set wine jars southeast of the chamber door in the hall, facing west ascending north.
Set wine jars southeast of the chamber door in the hall, facing north ascending west.
北向西上 means facing north with west as the superior rank, not facing west ascending north. The proposed literal corrects only that orientation phrase.
